variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A robotics agent is a system that turns a goal and sensor evidence into physical action. It observes the world, estimates what is happening, chooses a bounded next action, and sends that action through controllers to motors, wheels, or grippers.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Sense the current scene
pairs.detail: Timestamp camera, depth, force, position, velocity, and equipment signals.
pairs.explanation: Timestamp camera, depth, force, position, velocity, and equipment signals. Record sensor health and uncertainty instead of treating every reading as truth.

pairs.label: Estimate task state
pairs.detail: Fuse recent evidence into object poses, robot state, human proximity, and task progress.
pairs.explanation: Fuse recent evidence into object poses, robot state, human proximity, and task progress. Preserve ambiguity when several world states fit the observations.

pairs.label: Propose one bounded action
pairs.detail: A planner or vision-language-action policy selects a waypoint, grasp, tool call, or short action chunk that advances the goal.
pairs.explanation: A planner or vision-language-action policy selects a waypoint, grasp, tool call, or short action chunk that advances the goal.

pairs.label: Authorize and execute
pairs.detail: Independent checks reject stale, infeasible, or out-of-envelope proposals.
pairs.explanation: Independent checks reject stale, infeasible, or out-of-envelope proposals. A real-time controller converts an accepted proposal into actuator commands.

pairs.label: Compare outcome with intent
pairs.detail: Observe the real result, detect task success or divergence, update state, and replan.
pairs.explanation: Observe the real result, detect task success or divergence, update state, and replan. Never extend an old plan after the world has changed.

variants.hint:
Sense the current scene: Timestamp camera, depth, force, position, velocity, and equipment signals.

Estimate task state: Fuse recent evidence into object poses, robot state, human proximity, and task progress.

Propose one bounded action: A planner or vision-language-action policy selects a waypoint, grasp, tool call, or short action chunk that advances the goal.

Authorize and execute: Independent checks reject stale, infeasible, or out-of-envelope proposals.

Compare outcome with intent: Observe the real result, detect task success or divergence, update state, and replan.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A robotics agent is a system that turns a goal and sensor evidence into physical action. It observes the world, estimates what is happening, chooses a bounded next action, and sends that action through controllers to motors, wheels, or grippers.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Task and semantic planner
pairs.detail: Interprets the goal, orders skills, selects tools, and decides when the task is complete.
pairs.explanation: Interprets the goal, orders skills, selects tools, and decides when the task is complete. A multimodal reasoning model can help here because the loop tolerates deliberation.

pairs.label: Perception and action policy
pairs.detail: Turns current observations into object state, waypoints, or short action chunks.
pairs.explanation: Turns current observations into object state, waypoints, or short action chunks. A VLA policy may combine visual, language, and robot-state tokens.

pairs.label: Motion and servo control
pairs.detail: Tracks trajectories, regulates force, and talks to hardware.
pairs.explanation: Tracks trajectories, regulates force, and talks to hardware. This loop needs deterministic timing and must not wait for remote model inference.

pairs.label: Runtime safety supervisor
pairs.detail: Checks freshness, collision, geofence, speed, force, human proximity, and approved task state before and during execution.
pairs.explanation: Checks freshness, collision, geofence, speed, force, human proximity, and approved task state before and during execution.

pairs.label: Recovery and teleoperation
pairs.detail: Owns stop, retry, local fallback, human approval, and remote control.
pairs.explanation: Owns stop, retry, local fallback, human approval, and remote control. A handoff must never be the only response inside a short hazard window.

pairs.label: Evidence and operations
pairs.detail: Versions the executable stack, stores synchronized traces, measures drift, and proves each embodiment and operating-domain release.
pairs.explanation: Versions the executable stack, stores synchronized traces, measures drift, and proves each embodiment and operating-domain release.

Recovery and teleoperation: Owns stop, retry, local fallback, human approval, and remote control.

pairs.label: Replay and simulate broadly
pairs.detail: Sweep object, lighting, instruction, contact, timing, sensor, and network variations.
pairs.explanation: Sweep object, lighting, instruction, contact, timing, sensor, and network variations. Use counterfactual and fault-injection cases to find cheap failures.

pairs.label: Exercise the real stack
pairs.detail: Run software- and hardware-in-the-loop with production clocks, calibration, action transforms, controllers, limits, and communication paths.
pairs.explanation: Run software- and hardware-in-the-loop with production clocks, calibration, action transforms, controllers, limits, and communication paths.

pairs.label: Use guarded physical trials
pairs.detail: Begin at low energy with fixtures, exclusion zones, observers, emergency controls, and explicit stop criteria.
pairs.explanation: Begin at low energy with fixtures, exclusion zones, observers, emergency controls, and explicit stop criteria.

pairs.label: Expand one regime at a time
pairs.detail: Promote only demonstrated objects, environments, payloads, speeds, and recovery paths.
pairs.explanation: Promote only demonstrated objects, environments, payloads, speeds, and recovery paths. Keep rollback and operator authority available.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A robotics agent is a system that turns a goal and sensor evidence into physical action. It observes the world, estimates what is happening, chooses a bounded next action, and sends that action through controllers to motors, wheels, or grippers.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: End-to-end VLA policy
pairs.detail: Can transfer visual and language knowledge into generalist action proposals.
pairs.explanation: Can transfer visual and language knowledge into generalist action proposals. It is harder to debug, certify, and constrain, so keep the action horizon short and the authority boundary explicit.

pairs.label: Modular perception and planning
pairs.detail: Exposes object state, planner intent, and controller contracts.
pairs.explanation: Exposes object state, planner intent, and controller contracts. Interfaces can lose information, but failures and ownership are easier to isolate.

pairs.label: Remote intelligence
pairs.detail: Supports rich reasoning and fleet learning.
pairs.explanation: Supports rich reasoning and fleet learning. Latency, jitter, privacy, and connectivity require local safe behavior and a clear timeout.

pairs.label: On-device policy
pairs.detail: Keeps the action path close to the robot.
pairs.explanation: Keeps the action path close to the robot. Model size, heat, energy, update strategy, and hardware diversity become deployment constraints.

variants.hint:

Modular perception and planning: Exposes object state, planner intent, and controller contracts.

Remote intelligence: Supports rich reasoning and fleet learning.

On-device policy: Keeps the action path close to the robot.
